messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT 1716001234 - routing/fallback loop detected
incident-bot: symptom: health-check flapping observed across regions (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). automated fallback fired repeatedly.
pagerduty-bot: paging oncall: @maya (pager duty) :rotating_light:
maya: I'm on call, looking now. thanks for the ping. starting a quick triage.

jordan: jumping in — seeing repeated health probes fail in us-west (~every 10s) then traffic falling back to eu which then briefly fails and returns to us-east, creating a 3-hop loop.
maya: logs:
```
# sample svc-prober logs (trimmed)
2024-05-10T03:12:14Z probe(us-west)->200 OK latency=120ms
2024-05-10T03:12:24Z probe(us-west)->503 ServiceUnavailable
2024-05-10T03:12:25Z router: fallback to eu (variant: v1-quant)
2024-05-10T03:12:26Z probe(eu)->200 OK
2024-05-10T03:12:36Z probe(eu)->502 BadGateway
2024-05-10T03:12:37Z router: fallback to us-east (variant: v2-int8)
2024-05-10T03:12:38Z probe(us-east)->200 OK
2024-05-10T03:12:48Z probe(us-east)->503 ServiceUnavailable
```

liam: interesting - note the model variant differs per region (us-east: v2-int8, eu: v1-quant, us-west: v2-fp16). Could be a variant compatibility or probe expectation mismatch.

emma: customer impact: we've got elevated 5xxs for EU customers (region header eu-west) and p50 token latency up ~3x for a subset of requests. 3 paying customers reported spikes in last 20m.

samir: telemetry shows health-check threshold is set to 1 fail -> mark unhealthy. router policy has max_fallback_attempts = 0 (infinite until success) and cross-region backoff is short (5s). that's a recipe for a hop loop.
maya: plan proposal: 1) temporarily disable cross-region automatic fallback for the affected pool (keep local preferred). 2) raise health-check fail threshold to 3 consecutive fails. 3) set max_fallback_attempts=1 and add a 60s cooldown for region failover. 4) pin the three impacted customers to eu-only via route override.
jordan: agree. mitigation steps I'm executing now: disabling fallback for pool "inference-prod-ml-1" and increasing probe window. run commands: 
```
# disable cross-region fallback
redwoodctl routing update --pool inference-prod-ml-1 --cross-region-fallback=false
# increase health probe threshold
redwoodctl probes set --pool inference-prod-ml-1 --consecutive-failures 3
# set max fallback attempts
redwoodctl routing update --pool inference-prod-ml-1 --max-fallback-attempts 1 --fallback-cooldown 60s
```

maya: applied. confirm toggles?
jordan: toggles confirmed. watch logs for next 90s.

(1m pass)
liam: initial delta: 5xxs for eu dropped from 4.8% -> 1.1% in the first minute after change. no new hop chains in router logs.
emma: customer report: one of the 3 customers says latency normalized, others still seeing rare spikes but much improved.
samir: tracing shows the previous loop came from inconsistent probe responses across variant builds: eu variant sometimes returns 502 for the probe path /health?variant=probe-check due to a model-serving comp mismatch. we'll schedule a variant audit.

maya: next steps: 1) temp mitigation remains in place. 2) escalate to runtime team for variant alignment. 3) handoff to liam for the rest of my oncall window (30m) — I'll follow up with the post-incident note.

ryan: runtime action item: coordinate with model-onboarding to ensure probe endpoint is identical across variants and add a sanity check that model variant changes don't flip probe contract. Also add a short-term guard: if probe responses differ by content (not just code), treat as fail but do not immediate fallback.
jordan: filing incident ticket INC-20240510-27 with timeline and mitigation ticks.

maya: severity set to Sev2 (customer-facing error spike, partial degradation). notifying CS to proactively reach out to the 3 impacted customers.
emma: CS notified and drafting message.

samir: for postmortem: will include root cause hypothesis: (a) probe fragility + aggressive health thresholds + retry policy with no backoff -> region stomping; (b) model variant mismatch causing intermittent probe 502s. remediation: standardized probe contract, increase probe robustness, conservative fallback defaults (cooldown and max attempts), and an automated policy check before a new variant is rolled to production.
maya: handing pager to liam now. liam: taking it. ping me if escalates.

liam: acknowledged. I'll keep the mitigation until variant audit completed. please add any logs or customer notes to INC-20240510-27.

(incident-bot): incident state updated -> mitigated (temporary controls applied). will remain open for postmortem and follow-up tasks.

emma: ETA for permanent fix? runtime + model teams estimate 3 days to push consistent probe contract and 1 week to harden rollout checks. we'll aim for 72-hour follow-up.

maya: thanks everyone. closing this thread for active paging. postmortem assigned to samir/jordan.

--- end of thread ---
